The primary lane uses `createCss(preset)` with `css.class(...)` for class-string hosts and a static multi-map `css(...)` + `css.props(...)` tile host, compiled by the shipped `yumcssExtractVite(css)` plugin. The only runtime style value is the rating percentage custom property. Values are per-metric rankings; there is no cross-category score.

The CSS-in-JS Bench page does not call `cx()`, so it does not exercise the class-map compiler optimization. The current YumCSS SSR median reports a 33.7% spread. Its rank measures this fixture; it is not evidence for or against the `cx()` change.

The broader shared default-catalog proposal remains a no-go because the measured package and TypeScript costs did not establish a total win. ## Real-world CSS compiler: Emisoup

Pinned Emisoup source 005b44b87470228738873fd66076737a2017b3 on Vite 8.3.0 transformed 3,026 modules. Its three-build median was 7.24 s after versus 7.28 s before; spread prevents an end-to-end speedup claim. On a 1,000-file no-CSS workload, guarded discovery reduced the targeted parse-and-walk phase from 9.70 ms to 0.275 ms median, with parser calls dropping from 1,000 to 0. Playground also showed no build regression: 5.04 s after versus 5.61 s before over 4,220 modules.

Current package-build recheck measured 2026-09-25 on Apple M4 (arm64), macOS, Node 24.20.0, with Emisoup source a13301f9a663b2190cdfd9ac4969794b2c3d6b74 and YumCSS source 180ceaf1a8ab011f62e1a929fbc9a2c56f3da1e1. Five full build commands had medians of 5.91 s for Emisoup (5.67–7.04 s) and 12.39 s for Playground (11.66–17.41 s). These are variability samples, not a before/after speedup claim.

The production source-eligibility filter also fixes excluded modules leaking into CSS extraction. An instrumented Emisoup profile measured CSS `generateBundle` at 1.883 s before and 0.841 s after (about 55% lower across three warm runs per mode). Full-process Emisoup and Playground samples remain variable and establish no end-to-end speedup. Arena's current-output recheck preserves its measured metrics; CSS-in-JS Bench ranking remains tied to its pinned measured artifact. See the detailed comparison in [PERF.md](PERF.md#real-world-vite-extraction-emisoup-and-playground).

All emitted Emisoup client assets total 3,003,504 raw, 894,553 gzip-9, and 791,621 Brotli-11 bytes with each file compressed separately. The main YumCSS CSS asset is 123,976 raw, 21,169 gzip-9, and 18,496 Brotli-11 bytes. The progress-fill keeps static theme styles in CSS and width as a changing CSS variable; detailed hook, profile, CSS duplication, and delivery findings are in [PERF.md](PERF.md#real-world-vite-extraction-emisoup-and-playground).

## Benchmark cadence

Run focused regression benchmarks with changes to the compiler, runtime, public API, or bundler plugin paths they cover. Refresh the full local comparison before releases and monthly while performance work is active. Refresh external CSS-in-JS Bench/Arena comparisons quarterly, or sooner when a benchmarked library or its major version changes. A JJ revision by itself is not a reason to rerun the full matrix.

## Refresh

1. Run the local commands listed at the end of [PERF.md](PERF.md).
2. In a separate CSS-in-JS Bench checkout, run `pnpm gen:samples --measure=microbench,payload,buildtime`, then `pnpm gen:wpd`, `pnpm verify`, and `pnpm report`.
3. In CSS-in-JS Arena, refresh the pinned YumCSS tarball, pass the six-route geometry and screenshot gates, then run the byte, build, dev-start, four-sweep HMR, and scale measurements. Apply [the unique-scale fixture patch](benchmarks/css-in-js-arena/unique-scale-fixture.patch) before `tools/scale.mjs`; keep parity and source revisions with the results.
4. Import `BENCHMARK.json` with `node scripts/import-css-in-js-bench.mjs /path/to/BENCHMARK.json <yumcss-commit>`, update `benchmarks/css-in-js-arena/snapshot.json`, then run `pnpm run bench:summary` and `pnpm run bench:summary:check`.
